[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. [2] Project: Silhouette
The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: LexAI
LexAI is built with Gemini 2.5 Flash · Vercel Serverless · React 18 (CDN) · Node.js. Most people sign contracts they don't fully understand. Not because they're careless. Because contract review is genuinely hard, slow, and expensive if you want it done right. LexAI runs five agents on your contract. One figures out what kind of document it is. One summarizes your obligations. Two run in parallel: one grading every clause on fairness and clarity, one hunting for predatory terms. The fifth writes you counter-proposals with actual suggested wording. Full analysis in 15–25 seconds. The parallelism isn't a flex: it's what makes the wait time feel respectful of your time.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. [3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

The question I kept getting, implicitly, in every ML and AI role, was: do you actually understand what's happening underneath? So I answered it directly. Three systems demos, written in C, compiled to WebAssembly, running live in your browser right now. A free-list memory allocator with coalescing. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[4] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

PostHog Engineering Impact Dashboard is built with Python · Airflow · dbt · PostgreSQL · FastAPI · Redis · React · Vercel. Engineering teams generate a lot of data and almost no insight. Commits, PRs, reviews, issues: all happening, none of it connected. I wanted to know: what does a fair, comparable measure of engineering output actually look like? So I built the whole pipeline. Airflow pulls daily from GitHub, dbt shapes it into something meaningful across six models, FastAPI serves it, Redis caches it with hit/miss transparency, and a React dashboard renders it: leaderboards, trend charts, a custom impact score I designed myself (because the formula matters as much as the infrastructure). The interesting part wasn't the stack. It was deciding what to measure and why.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[7] Project: Silhouette
Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[9] Project: Silhouette
The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. One Redis instance. [3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

What is Silhouette about?

Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[7] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[2] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. [3] Project: Silhouette
Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[3] Project: PostHog Engineering Impact Dashboard
PostHog Engineering Impact Dashboard is built with Python · Airflow · dbt · PostgreSQL · FastAPI · Redis · React · Vercel. Engineering teams generate a lot of data and almost no insight. Commits, PRs, reviews, issues: all happening, none of it connected. I wanted to know: what does a fair, comparable measure of engineering output actually look like? So I built the whole pipeline. Airflow pulls daily from GitHub, dbt shapes it into something meaningful across six models, FastAPI serves it, Redis caches it with hit/miss transparency, and a React dashboard renders it: leaderboards, trend charts, a custom impact score I designed myself (because the formula matters as much as the infrastructure). The interesting part wasn't the stack. It was deciding what to measure and why.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

PostHog Engineering Impact Dashboard is built with Python · Airflow · dbt · PostgreSQL · FastAPI · Redis · React · Vercel. Engineering teams generate a lot of data and almost no insight. Commits, PRs, reviews, issues: all happening, none of it connected. I wanted to know: what does a fair, comparable measure of engineering output actually look like? So I built the whole pipeline. Airflow pulls daily from GitHub, dbt shapes it into something meaningful across six models, FastAPI serves it, Redis caches it with hit/miss transparency, and a React dashboard renders it: leaderboards, trend charts, a custom impact score I designed myself (because the formula matters as much as the infrastructure). The interesting part wasn't the stack. It was deciding what to measure and why.
